newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rates slip back to usual level.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rates slip back to usual level.

text.p: Dutch call money rates edged lower on Thursday after recent highs and dealers saw more volatility in overnight money though giving no explicit reason for the movements.
Call money was bid at 3.00 percent, on a similar level as the current special advances rate, compared to 3.25 to 3.50 percent on Wednesday and an occasional higher settlement the previous day.
One dealer said call money had been at a high level recently because some players were still not completely used to the new money market instruments.
Another dealer said that he had the idea that some big banks had been holding on to their liquidity, which meant more tightness for smaller banks.
"But, I do not have a clue why they were holding on to it," the dealer added.
"Call money will probably remain volatile in the near future," he said, with another saying the direction was unclear.
Dealers were unanimous on today's announcement of the new special advances pact, saying the rate would remain unchanged at 3.00 percent when the central bank announces a new pact at 1400 GMT.
Last week the central bank raised the special advances pact to support the guilder versus the German mark as the guilder was trading at 112.60 per 100 marks on July 10.
The guilder was a little stronger today, trading at 112.59 per 100 marks.
"The central bank might raise the special advances pact again if the guilder weakens to 112.67 per 100 marks or further," the dealer said, but he added the chance of a rate rise was very thin.
"The Dutch central bank is keen to leave the special advances rate level with the German repo rate," he said.
